# Judith Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_001_page_001.jpg

---

**1** This is the story of what happened in the twelfth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign. He called himself king of the Assyrians and ruled from Nineveh, that great city. Meanwhile, far to the east, a king named Arphaxad held power over the Medes from his capital at Ecbatana.

**2** Arphaxad had fortified Ecbatana with formidable walls — massive hewn stones, each three cubits thick and six cubits long, rising seventy cubits high and fifty cubits wide.

**3** He crowned the city gates with towers a hundred cubits tall, each sixty cubits wide at the base.

**4** The gates themselves soared seventy cubits high and stretched forty cubits across — wide enough to pour out his armies in battle formation.

**5** It was against this fortified king that Nebuchadnezzar marched. The two powers clashed on the broad plain near the borders of Ragae.

**6** Arphaxad was not alone. The hill tribes rallied to him. The peoples of the Euphrates valley, the Tigris, the Hydaspes, and the plain of Arioch — all came together under Arioch king of the Elymaeans. Scores of nations under the sons of Cheloud joined the fight.

**7** Nebuchadnezzar had sent his summons west — to Persia, to all the western territories: Cilicia, Damascus, Lebanon, Anti-Lebanon, and every nation clinging to the seacoast.

**8** He summoned Carmel and Gilead, Upper Galilee, the broad valley of Esdraelon.

**9** He sent word to Samaria and all its towns, across the Jordan to Jerusalem, to Betane, Chelous, Kadesh, the Egyptian frontier — Tahpanhes, Rameses, the whole land of Goshen —

**10** all the way to Tanis and Memphis, and south through Egypt to the borders of Ethiopia.

**11** Every last one of them ignored him. The peoples of the whole western world refused to mobilize. They had no fear of Nebuchadnezzar — he was just one man among many, nothing special. They sent his envoys packing, empty-handed and humiliated.

**12** That was a catastrophic miscalculation. Nebuchadnezzar flew into a rage. He swore on his throne and his crown: every nation that defied him would pay. Cilicia, Damascus, Syria — the sword. Moab, Ammon, Judea, Egypt — the sword. From one sea to the other, he would make them all pay.

**13** He turned first to settle the score with Arphaxad. In the seventeenth year of his reign he crushed him — shattered his cavalry, smashed his chariots, routed his entire army.

**14** He took Arphaxad's cities one by one. He marched into Ecbatana, seized its towers, looted its markets, and ground its splendor into the dust.

**15** He ran Arphaxad himself to ground in the mountains of Ragae and killed him with his own spear.

**16** Then he turned for home, his enormous host trailing behind him — soldiers and camp followers and plunder. Back in Nineveh, he and his army spent the next four months in celebration.
